key_insight: MyoCardBench is a large real-world benchmark designed to test how well LLMs handle the full, clinically authentic cardiovascular care workflow rather than isolated exam-style tasks.
clinical_relevance: The benchmark helps identify where medical LLMs perform well versus where they miss critical cardiology details, which is important for safer, more reliable support in cardiovascular care settings.
method: Built 2,263 items from 13 task-specific datasets using de-identified cardiovascular records and exam data.
16 cardiology physicians created annotations and reference answers, with cross-review by 2 senior cardiologists.
Seven LLMs produced 15,841 outputs under standardized zero-shot evaluation across multiple clinical dimensions.
evidence_signal: GPT-5.4 had the top macro-average score (62.55) and item-weighted mean (62.19), while performance varied widely by task, from CardioAuxReport (86.38) down to CardioECGRead (17.25) and CardioEthics (17.34).
watch_item: Because the benchmark is zero-shot and based on retrospective de-identified data, results may not fully predict performance in real-time clinical workflows or with local practice variation.
paper_title: MyoCardBench: A Real-World Data Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Clinically Authentic Cardiovascular Care Scenarios
